African digital financial services platform Airtel Money plans to list existing shares on the London Stock Exchange but won't raise new capital.
Airtel Money, also known as Airtel Mobile Commerce, said Wednesday that the shares would be sold by existing shareholders and that upon admission it expects it will have a free float of at least 10%.

As part of the sale, International Finance Corp. agreed to buy a stake of up to 67.2 million pounds, equivalent to $89.7 million, from shareholders. Shares will also be offered to U.K. residents, with the full details of the offer price expected in mid-October, it said.
Airtel Africa, which owns 77.85% of Airtel Money's shares, said in a separate release that it expects to remain a long-term shareholder.
Airtel Money operates in 13 markets in Sub-Saharan Africa, where traditional banking infrastructure is underdeveloped.
